summary.headline: IMFA Q4 FY26 production about 68,500 t and PAT rose to INR103 crore on realisations of about INR109,000/t, though forex MTM weighed on other expenses.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as operationally strong, with production of about 68,500 tonnes including roughly 2,200 tonnes from the KNR 2 acquisition (closed 27 February 2026, furnaces switched on in March). Realisations rose to about INR109,000/t from about INR87,000/t a year earlier, lifting PAT to about INR103 crore from INR47 crore. Reported other expenses were hit by a notional forex mark-to-market loss of about INR28 crore on hedges (actual loss about INR3 crore), with the company stating the underlying forex gain sits in revenue. Management guided Q1 FY27 margins and prices above Q4 and expects around 80,000 t of sales in Q1 versus a normal 65,000–67,000 t.

segments.name: Ferro alloys (ferrochrome)
segments.commentary: Export sales are about 90% of volume, all in dollars. Management targets a 60:40 export:domestic mix by around late FY27, with at least about 200,000 t allocated domestically over time. Domestic prices are cited at INR118,000–120,000/t and export realisations above INR120,000/t.

segments.name: Mining
segments.commentary: Chrome ore output was about 8 lakh t in FY26 (above 7 lakh t in FY25), with FY27 target of 10 lakh t. Mahagari underground output was 536,000 t, and the long-term plan is 12 lakh t, entirely underground, under an investment of close to INR1,000 crore.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Existing power base is 200 MW thermal at Choudwar, 4.5 MW solar at Therubali and about 5 MW off-gas. Hybrid renewable of 135 MW is contracted: 70 MW from JSW Energy (around July 2026) and 65 MW from Enfinity Global (June 2027); the 40 MW earlier deal was cancelled. The company expects 35–40% of energy from renewables in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ferrochrome output indicated at about 400,000 t, rising to about 475,000–500,000 t in FY28 (KNR 1 and KNR 2 combined).

KNR 1 (100,000 t greenfield) furnaces to be switched on around 10–15 July 2026, with the second furnace around end-August/early September; annualised 500,000 t run-rate targeted by November–December 2026.
Ethanol project: commissioning in Q2 FY27 with output expected around end-August 2026.
Partially built 33 MVA furnace at KNR 2 (adds about 50,000 t) targeted for June 2027, subject to environmental clearance; firm timeline to be given with Q1 results.
EBITDA cost per ton to fall INR3,000–4,000/t on a weighted basis once KNR 1 and KNR 2 are fully running; steady state expected from Q4 FY27.

FY27 capex about INR450 crore (balance Kalinganagar, ethanol and Sukinda underground mines), funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan plus internal accruals; FY28 mines capex about INR700 crore, with the bulk likely in FY28.
Coal linkage pricing expected to be INR400–500/t cheaper, benefiting from H2 FY27.
Q1 FY27: sales about 80,000 t; prices and margins guided above Q4 FY26; Q2 prices expected to be similar to Q1.
capex_capacity: KNR 1 greenfield (100,000 t): cold trials and pre-commissioning from 30 May 2026; start delayed 10–15 days due to partial manpower demobilisation and heat.
KNR 2 acquired from Tata Steel, closed 27 February 2026; operating at about 70% utilisation per analyst. Furnace tally: 100,000 t acquired plus 50,000 t from the partially built 33 MVA furnace.
Ethanol plant: pre-commissioning July 2026, commissioning Q2 FY27.
Chrome mining: 10 lakh t in FY27, moving to 12 lakh t; Sukinda open-cast ore (3–4 lakh t) to taper into underground output of about 6 lakh t.
Possible third furnace at KNR 1 on land already held; decision deferred. The earlier 220,000 t phase 2 expansion is no longer being pursued.
demand_pricing: Global ferrochrome output fell about 9.4% to just under 16 million t in 2025, supporting firmer prices along with elevated cost structures.
South African power tariff: special rate of $0.62/kWh approved versus $1.36 standard (earlier $0.877). Management views the net effect on IMFA as neutral; the outcome is uncertain.
West Asia crisis: direct impact limited to higher freight and domestic logistics costs; container and shipping availability described as under control.

Hedging policy: about 25–30% of net forex exposure hedged, mostly forwards for 12–18 months. Rupee moved from about INR89.9 (31 Dec) to INR93.65–94.65 (31 Mar) and about INR95–96 at the time of the call.
Marketing: about 70–75% of volume under long-term contracts (monthly pricing for China, quarterly for POSCO and Japanese customers); the balance is repeat spot sales.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of South African power tariff relief and the global supply response on Asian ferrochrome competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if South African output rises, Chinese ore supply may fall, so net supply is roughly neutral; it flagged possible upside-sharing conditions and that the tariff may not be viable if prices drop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total power requirement met by hybrid renewables and the cost saving?
qa_highlights.answer: Power need for KNR 1 and KNR 2 is about 100 MW; 135 MW is contracted (70 MW from July 2026 and 65 MW from June 2027). Renewable tariffs are at about grid parity, fixed for 25–29 years, and coal linkage savings of INR400–500/t are expected from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and debt plans for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR450 crore, funded by about INR170 crore unutilised term loan and internal accruals. FY28 includes about INR700 crore for mines, with the exact amount not yet calculated.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy and the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: About 25–30% of exposure is hedged for 12–18 months. The notional MTM loss is about INR28 crore against an actual loss of about INR3 crore, while the forex gain in revenue is about INR80 crore above budget for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,000–4,000/t EBITDA cost saving from KNR appear in current numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: The saving applies only once both KNR 1 and KNR 2 are running. Start-up costs and CTU fixed charges (about INR2–2.5 crore for the GNA RE corridor from 1 June) will ease over a few quarters, with full benefits from about November–December 2026 and steady state from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the export:domestic mix and H1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The company aims for 60:40 export:domestic by about late FY27 (currently 90:10). Q1 FY27 sales are about 80,000 t, with prices above Q4; Q2 is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Plans beyond ferrochrome, including critical minerals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing critical minerals and rare earths adjacent to its mining skill set. It has bought tender documents for some blocks in Odisha and elsewhere but has not yet bid. No quantified timeline was given.

risks_watch: KNR 1 furnace commissioning slippage (currently 10–15 July) due to manpower and temperatures of 44–45°C.
Environmental clearance for the KNR 2 33 MVA furnace; the June 2027 target is not firm.
Rupee volatility driving notional forex MTM losses on the 25–30% hedged book; Q1 FY27 may see more if INR stays at about INR95–96.
South African tariff outcome and possible supply response; potential price pressure if South African output rises.
Start-up inefficiencies (heat-up of 10–12 days, DISCOM power cost until 80–90% load) affecting near-term EBITDA per ton.
Ethanol project delivery (Q2 FY27 commissioning) and the Tata Steel KNR 2 integration.
Cash and investment income declining after the acquisition (cash down to about INR400–450 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and near-term Q1 FY27 numbers, but deliberately cautious on the medium term: management declined to give EBITDA-per-ton targets or price forecasts beyond about two quarters. It was candid about project slippage (KNR 1, ethanol) and about the notional nature of the forex loss, while giving few numbers on critical minerals and the South African tariff.
key_quotes: So, we will be looking at allocating at least about 200,000 tons to the domestic market in times to come.
I would say that the fourth quarter of FY '26 has been a very good quarter operationally.
Of course, a lot of it is notional, not realized, not actual losses.
